software: SafetyCulture (now Mitti by SafetyCulture, formerly iAuditor)
title: Rugged tablet for SafetyCulture (Mitti, iAuditor)
meta_description: Which Tuga rugged Android tablet runs the Mitti (by SafetyCulture) app: Android 10 minimum, offline inspections, in-app QR scanning, UK pricing.
h1: Rugged tablet for SafetyCulture (Mitti, formerly iAuditor)
intro: SafetyCulture is the inspection and workplace operations platform that maintenance, engineering, facilities and health and safety teams use for digital checklists, inspections and audits, issue reporting, task management and asset maintenance. The vendor lists Manufacturing, Facilities Management, Construction, Retail and Hospitality as its industries, says the platform is used across more than 18,000 UK businesses, and publishes UK customer stories from National Grid UK, William Hare (bringing 6,000 assets onto the platform), Edinburgh Airport and Motor Fuel Group. The naming has changed twice: the app was iAuditor, was renamed SafetyCulture in November 2022, and the company rebranded as Mitti on 11 August 2026. The app is now listed in Google Play and the App Store as Mitti (by SafetyCulture), and the Android package is still com.safetyculture.iauditor.

On the floor or on site, a technician opens the mobile app, runs a pre-use check or scheduled inspection, scans a QR code or barcode with the app's built-in scanner to pull up an asset, photographs defects, raises actions and carries on without signal. The vendor documents offline use of inspections, assets, actions, documents and schedules in the mobile app, with automatic sync when the device is back online. That is a job for a device with an ingress protection rating and a wide operating temperature range rather than a consumer tablet: the Tuga A10 is rated IP68 and MIL-STD-810H and operates from -20 to 60C, and the A6 is rated IP67 with a 1.5 metre drop rating and operates from -20 to 50C.

This page sets out what the vendor publishes about devices for Mitti, which Tuga device fits the Android app, where the Windows W10 does and does not fit, how to get the app running, and the commercial terms for UK business buyers.

requirements.detail: The vendor's supported devices article states a minimum of Android 10.0 with 4GB RAM or more for phones and tablets. It recommends Android 16.0 or above on tablets equivalent to a Galaxy Tab S9 or A9 or better, and app version 26.32 or later. Chrome OS is not supported.

The app is listed on Google Play as Mitti (by SafetyCulture), developer SafetyCulture, package com.safetyculture.iauditor, updated 4 October 2026, with 1m+ downloads and a PEGI 3 rating. The listing does not display a Requires Android value, so the minimum version above comes from the vendor help centre. The vendor also publishes a direct APK (help article 000095) for devices that cannot reach Google Play.

Offline is supported in the mobile app only. Offline features are Actions, Assets, Documents, Inspections, Issues, Reports, Schedule and Training. Analytics, Heads Up, Lone Worker, Supply, Notifications, Library, Sensors and the Template Editor are not available offline. The app syncs automatically when back online, with a manual sync option, and the vendor advises checking sync status before going offline.

Barcode and QR code scanner questions are answered with the app's built-in scanner, and the vendor states that barcodes can only be scanned via the mobile app. It reads QR codes and the 1D and 2D barcodes EAN-13/UPC-A, UPC-E, EAN-8, Code 128, Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5. The article does not mention external or Bluetooth barcode scanners.

Assets can be created from RFID tags in the Android mobile app using a Zebra RFID scanner connected over Bluetooth. The vendor requires mobile app 25.24 or higher, Android 8 or above, the Assets: Manage permission, a full seat and the device online. Specific Zebra models are not named, and the article does not mention NFC.

Inspections can capture readings from supported Bluetooth thermometers, pH meters, paint thickness gauges and oil quality testers. This is a mobile app feature and requires a Premium or Enterprise plan.

There is no native Windows app. The vendor's FAQ states that as of 14 July 2022 the Mitti Windows app ceased to function and recommends the web app or an Android or iOS device. The same FAQ states that offline access is unsupported on the web app, which requires a consistent internet connection. The vendor's browser article lists Windows among the web app's operating systems and recommends Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge (help article 002418).
The mobile app can be logged in on up to three mobile devices at once, and device limits are specific to each organisation, which matters when a team shares a pool of tablets.

recommended.why: Mitti's technician features (offline inspections, barcode and QR scanning, RFID asset creation, Bluetooth instrument readings) are mobile app features, and the Android app is the route the vendor documents for them. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with 8GB RAM, which meets the published minimum of Android 10.0 and 4GB. It does not meet the vendor's recommended tier of Android 16.0 on Galaxy Tab S9 or A9 class hardware, so expect the app to run within the supported range rather than at the recommended specification. The A10 gives a 10.1 inch screen for checklists and photos, IP68 and MIL-STD-810H ratings for the shop floor and site, 4G dual SIM for sync away from Wi-Fi, and a pogo pin connector for a charging or vehicle dock. It is the device an industrial asset-management firm has already bought from us for maintenance technicians at an aerospace manufacturer, running a different maintenance app.
fit: Vendor minimum Android 10.0 (help article 000088): the A10 runs Android 14.
Vendor minimum 4GB RAM or more: the A10 has 8GB RAM, 128GB storage and microSD up to 2TB for offline inspection data and photos.

Barcode and QR scanning through the app's built-in scanner, mobile app only (help article 000069): the A10 has a 13MP rear camera with flash. The A10 has no dedicated scan engine, so in-app scanning depends on the app using the camera.
RFID asset creation uses a Zebra RFID scanner over Bluetooth (help article 005535): the A10 has Bluetooth 5.2.
Offline inspections with automatic sync when back online (help article 002907): the A10 has 4G dual SIM, dual-band Wi-Fi 5 and an 8000mAh battery, with an operating range of -20 to 60C.

recommended.why: The Tuga A8 (£379, £70 less than the A10) is the middle size, with an 8 inch 1280 x 800 IPS screen that shows more of a checklist than a handheld and a 1000 nit panel for outdoor and sunlit inspections. It runs Android 12 with 6GB RAM, so it meets the vendor's minimum of Android 10.0 and 4GB RAM or more with some memory headroom, but like the A10 and A6 it does not meet the recommended Android 16.0 tier. The 8000mAh battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over mid shift, and VESA mount points and a pogo pin connector suit mounting or docking in a vehicle. The trade-offs against the A10 are IP67 rather than IP68, no MIL-STD rating, an older Android version, a lower screen resolution and 6GB RAM against 8GB, so trial one unit with your heaviest templates before a fleet order.
fit: Vendor minimum Android 10.0 (help article 000088): the A8 runs Android 12.
Vendor minimum 4GB RAM or more: the A8 has 6GB RAM, 128GB storage and a microSD slot for offline inspection data and photos.

Barcode and QR scanning through the app's built-in scanner, mobile app only (help article 000069): the A8 has a 13MP autofocus rear camera with flash and no dedicated scan engine, so in-app scanning depends on the app using the camera.
RFID asset creation uses a Zebra RFID scanner over Bluetooth (help article 005535): the A8 has Bluetooth.
Offline inspections with automatic sync when back online (help article 002907): the A8 has 4G LTE dual SIM, Wi-Fi and a removable 8000mAh battery.

recommended.why: The Tuga A6 is the pick when technicians need a handheld that fits a pocket or belt holster. It runs Android 15 with 4GB RAM, so it meets the vendor's minimum of Android 10.0 and 4GB RAM or more, but only just on memory: 4GB is the floor of the supported range, not headroom, and like the A10 it does not meet the recommended Android 16.0 tier. Trial one unit with your heaviest templates before a fleet order. The vendor publishes no screen-size guidance for the app and groups devices only as phones or tablets by model, so the choice between a 6 inch handheld and a 10.1 inch tablet is about how your team works, not about the published requirement. At 277g, with IP67 sealing, a 1.5 metre drop rating and a removable 5050mAh battery that can be swapped for a charged spare, it suits long walk-round shifts. It also has a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine, but the vendor documents scanning through the app's own camera scanner and does not mention external scanners, so test whether the app accepts the scan keys before relying on them.
fit: Vendor minimum Android 10.0: the A6 runs Android 15.
Vendor minimum 4GB RAM or more: the A6 has exactly 4GB RAM, so it meets the minimum with no margin, plus 64GB storage and microSD up to 256GB.

Barcode and QR scanning through the app's built-in scanner in the mobile app: the A6 has a 13MP rear camera with flash. It also has a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine, which the vendor does not document, so test it with the app.
Automatic sync when back online, Wi-Fi only or Wi-Fi and cellular (help article 000034): the A6 has 4G dual SIM, dual-band Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.1 for a Zebra RFID reader.
Handheld form for technicians on the move: 6 inch FHD+ 2160 x 1080 screen, 277g, IP67, 1.5 metre drop rating, removable 5050mAh battery.

recommended.why: The Tuga W10 is not a technician device for Mitti. The vendor has no native Windows app and documents the Windows route as the web app in Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge, with no offline access. Barcode and QR scanning, Bluetooth instrument readings and RFID asset creation are documented for the mobile app only. Where the W10 fits is as a docked or office unit for web app work: creating asset profile QR codes (help article 002882), building templates and adding scanner questions (help article 000069), and the modules the vendor lists as unavailable offline, such as Analytics and the Template Editor (help article 002907), over Ethernet or Wi-Fi in a plant room or workshop. Buy it for that, not for inspections on the floor.
fit: Web app on Windows in Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge (help article 002418): the W10 runs Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N100 with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage.
Web app requires a consistent internet connection (help article 000094): the W10 has 100Mbps RJ45 Ethernet and dual-band Wi-Fi 5, with optional 4G LTE.

Web app tasks such as creating asset profile QR codes and building templates (help articles 002882 and 000069): 10.1 inch IPS 1280 x 800 multi-touch display and HDMI out for a larger monitor at a desk or dock.
Workshop or plant room use: IP65 (dust tight and protected against water jets, not rated for immersion), removable 5000mAh battery, pogo pin dock connector for the £49.99 charging dock.

not_recommended_note: Three honest caveats. First, the Tuga A10, A8 and A6 meet the vendor's published minimum (Android 10.0, 4GB RAM) but not its recommended tier (Android 16.0 on Galaxy Tab S9 or A9 class or above), and we do not claim otherwise; the A6's 4GB RAM is exactly the minimum, so it has no memory headroom. Second, Windows support is browser-only: the vendor states the web app has no offline access and that barcodes can only be scanned via the mobile app, so the W10 is only suitable for web app work over a connection. Its optional 2D barcode scanner and UHF RFID reader modules have no documented use with Mitti, because the vendor documents scanning and RFID for the mobile app only. Third, barcode and QR scanning on the A10, A8 and A6 is done by the app's built-in scanner through the camera; the A6's built-in Zebra 2D scan engine has no documented use with Mitti, and the vendor's scanner article does not mention external barcode scanners. Two features are documented for iOS only (weather details, help article 003317, and distance estimates, help article 001801), the sync diagnostics setting is not available on Android (help article 000034), and the RFID workflow is documented with an external Zebra reader; the vendor does not document any use of a device's built-in NFC.
setup_steps: Create a Mitti account at mitti.com or use your organisation's existing one. The Free plan covers teams of up to 10 with 5 active inspection templates; Premium is priced per seat per month and Enterprise is custom priced. Prices on the vendor's pricing page are shown in dollars, and we found no GBP price list.

On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, install Mitti (by SafetyCulture) from Google Play (package com.safetyculture.iauditor). If the device cannot reach Google Play, the vendor publishes a direct APK in help article 000095; Android will ask you to allow installs from unknown sources.
Sign in with the technician's seat. The mobile app can be logged in on up to three mobile devices at once per organisation (help article 000058), so plan device allocation for shared pools.

Review the app's syncing settings before the first shift (help article 000034): offline inspections are on by default, and you can set the sync interval, Wi-Fi only or Wi-Fi and cellular, offline assets, offline schedules and the inspection storage limit (default one week). Check sync status before going offline.

If you create assets from RFID tags, pair a Zebra RFID scanner to the tablet over Bluetooth. The vendor requires app 25.24 or higher, Android 8 or above, the Assets: Manage permission and an online device for this workflow (help article 005535).

Fit the A10 to a £49.99 charging dock at the workshop or a £109 vehicle mounting dock in the van, both using the pogo pin connector. A hand strap is included in the A10 box; the A6 takes the £22 belt holster.

faq.q: Will the Tuga A10 run the SafetyCulture app, now called Mitti?
faq.a: The vendor's supported devices article requires Android 10.0 or above with 4GB RAM or more. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with 8GB RAM, so it meets that requirement. The vendor recommends Android 16.0 on Galaxy Tab S9 or A9 class tablets for the best experience, and the A10 does not reach that recommended tier. The app on Google Play is Mitti (by SafetyCulture), package com.safetyculture.iauditor.

faq.q: Does it work offline on site?
faq.a: Yes, in the mobile app. The vendor lists Actions, Assets, Documents, Inspections, Issues, Reports, Schedule and Training as available offline, with automatic sync when the device is back online and a manual sync option. Analytics, Heads Up, the Template Editor and some other modules need a connection. The web app, which is the only route on the Windows W10, has no offline access.

faq.q: Can we trial one unit before ordering for the whole team, and do you invoice businesses?
faq.a: Yes to both. A single trial unit before a fleet order is welcome, with 30-day returns and a 12-month warranty. Business buyers can request a quote and pay by bank transfer on a proforma invoice. Tuga Hardware is not VAT registered, so there is no VAT to add to the £449 A10, £379 A8, £349 A6 or £649 W10. Multi-unit discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 units, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more. Delivery is free worldwide in 7 to 10 working days.

faq.q: Should we choose the 10.1 inch A10 or the 6 inch A6?
faq.a: The vendor publishes no screen-size guidance and groups devices only as phones or tablets by model, so both meet the same Android 10.0 and 4GB minimum, the A10 with 8GB RAM and the A6 with exactly 4GB. Choose the A10 (10.1 inch FHD, 8GB RAM, 680g, 4G, IP68, pogo pin for a dock) where technicians fill in long checklists, review photos and work from a van or workstation dock. Choose the A6 (6 inch FHD+, 277g, 4G, IP67, removable battery, built-in Zebra 2D scan engine) where they need a pocketable handheld for walk-round checks across a large site, and trial it first given its minimum-level RAM.

faq.q: What about the Windows Tuga W10?
faq.a: There is no native Windows app; the vendor's FAQ says the Windows app ceased to function on 14 July 2022 and points Windows users to the web app, which its browser article supports in Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge. The web app has no offline access, and the vendor states barcodes can only be scanned via the mobile app. The W10 therefore suits office or dock-based web app work such as template building, asset QR code creation and analytics over its RJ45 Ethernet or Wi-Fi, not inspections on the floor.
